title: Readability: early return in delete
bug: Authors can't delete their posts, and anyone can delete everyone else's.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff inverts the authorization check from '!=' to '==', causing the post author (alice_admin) to receive 403 instead of 204, which the PR description does not announce.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The inverted condition now allows non-authors (erin_delete_others) to delete posts (204) instead of receiving 403, a behavior change not announced in the PR description.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: After the faulty delete succeeds for erin_delete_others, the post is removed, so a subsequent GET returns 404 instead of 200, an unintended side effect of the logic inversion.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff inverts the authorization check from '!=' to '==', causing the post author (alice_admin) to receive 403 instead of 204, which the PR description does not announce.

findings.label: needs_human
findings.why: The OAuth HTML form fields changed but the diff only touches the delete endpoint; the relationship is unclear and requires human investigation.

findings.label: needs_human
findings.why: The GET /api/posts latency increased significantly but the diff only modifies the delete endpoint; the cause is not evident from the given changes.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR inverts the authorization logic in DELETE /posts/<id>, causing authors to be forbidden and non-authors to delete posts, with cascading 404s; unrelated OAuth and latency changes need human review.

suspicions.claim: The authorization check is inverted: authors can no longer delete their own posts, while non-authors can delete any post.
suspicions.trigger:
1. Create user A and user B. 2. Log in as A, POST /api/posts with text to create post P (note id). 3. DELETE /api/posts/

with A's token -> expect 204 before PR, now 403. 4. DELETE /api/posts/

with B's token -> expect 403 before PR, now 204 (post deleted). 5. GET /api/posts/

to confirm deletion.
suspicions.evidence: DELETE /api/posts/1 with user A's token returned 204 in base and 403 in head, showing the author can no longer delete their own post.

suspicions.claim: When DISABLE_AUTH=true, the current user defaults to id=1; the inverted check lets user 1 delete only posts they do NOT own, and prevents them from deleting their own posts.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Set DISABLE_AUTH=true. 2. Ensure user 1 exists and owns post P1, user 2 owns post P2. 3. DELETE /api/posts/<P1> (no auth header) -> expect 204 before PR, now 403. 4. DELETE /api/posts/<P2> (no auth header) -> expect 403 before PR, now 204. 5. GET /api/posts/<P1> and /api/posts/<P2> to verify which was deleted.
suspicions.evidence: DELETE /api/posts/{p1_id} and DELETE /api/posts/{p2_id} both returned 404 in base and head because the placeholder post IDs were not resolved, so the authorization logic was never reached.
